documents.unit: Office of Research and Innovation, AI (ORAI)
documents.title: AI Guidelines & Principles (University Guidelines and Academic Integrity)
documents.summary: The university AI office page says there is no single university-wide AI policy, so use of AI in coursework falls under the Code of Academic Integrity. Students may use AI only with explicit instructor approval, instructors are urged to put expectations in the syllabus, and sample Red-Yellow-Green language is offered.
documents.stance_why: The page says students 'may only use AI tools for class assignments if your instructor has explicitly approved their use' and that unapproved use 'may violate the Code of Academic Integrity'. AI is banned unless permitted, which is restrict, even though instructors choose whether to permit; there are no stated tiers on this page itself. Reconciliation: coder B coded delegates because instructors choose; the page itself states a default for students ('may only use AI tools for class assignments if your instructor has explicitly approved their use'), which is restrict, and the sample Red-Yellow-Green text is an offered template, not a set of tiers on this page.

units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin, B coded all. The sentence is the university stating what it champions about its own guidelines, so the binding party is the university (admin).
units.anchor: champions practices that are legally sound, ethically grounded, and academically rigorous

notes: Two coders (A, B) coded independently and were reconciled. The PDF version of the College of Information Science policy (arizona-infosci-academic-integrity-pdf) is not in the output: both coders found its saved text to be a '404 Page Not Found' page, and the same policy is coded from the HTML page. The collect file should be rechecked or the PDF re-collected. Course layer was deferred in the collect file. The 2023 syllabus guidance (arizona-ucatt-syllabus-guidance) partly overlaps the current Instructor AI Policy Guide; both are coded separately. Coder B listed the 'list of LLMs with secure, FERPA-compliant environment, incl. Claude' as its own unit. It is a parenthetical inside the same sentence as the 'highly recommended to limit AI use to tools with U of A subscriptions' unit and adds no separate rule, so it was dropped. Units coded UNCOVERED: AI summarising of readings banned; instructor workload burden of disallowing AI; instructors must keep misconduct case information confidential; denying credit for unmet assignment requirements without a misconduct charge; students must distinguish when technology helps from when it replaces learning.
